newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Declaration bars WTO mandate on trade-labour link.
newsitem.headline: Declaration bars WTO mandate on trade-labour link.

text.p: Friday's closing declaration of the first ministerial meeting of the World Trade Organisation does not give the WTO a mandate to examine the link between trade and core labour standards, the meeting's chairman said.
Singaporean trade minister Yeo Cheow Tong, reading a statement agreed by fellow ministers, said the ministerial declaration set out a balanced framework for dealing with the highly contentious issue.

After summarising the agreed text on workplace standards, Yeo told the final plenary session of the meeting: "Some delegations had expressed a concern that this text may lead the WTO to acquire a competence to undertake further work in the relationship between trade and core labour standards.
"I want to assure these delegations that this text will not permit such a development."
His comments reflected the deep fears of developing countries that the trade advantage they enjoy from low wages would be blunted if rich nations succeeded in imposing global labour standards.

But the chairman's statement, for all the force of its language, is not binding on WTO members and the United States has said it intends to keep up its campaign for action to stamp out child labour and improve sweatshop conditions.
The ministerial declaration says that the International Labour Organisation is the competent body to deal with workplace standards and rejects the use of them for protectionist purposes.
"This is a very important safeguard for the multilateral trading system and in particular for developing countries," Yeo said.
